host.runtimeVersion: container CLI version 1.1.0 (build: release, commit: unspeci)
host.systemStart: apiserver was already running; no system start was needed

proves: a real legacy-only container is drained, deleted, and recreated carrying both ownership namespaces
the named volume it held is proven released before the replacement attaches it, and is re-attached to the replacement at the same destination
data written inside that named volume survives the container being deleted and recreated, and survives a subsequent restart
the migrated container is still discoverable by the pre-migration reader predicate (rollback contract)
a container an operator left stopped is replaced stopped; a running one is stopped gracefully and replaced running
a conflicting container anywhere on the host stops the sweep with zero mutations, and the probe survives the refusal with its volume attached
a migrated container is skipped by a second sweep rather than migrated twice
containers outside the named target set do not change ownership class
doesNotProve: migration of named volumes or networks; those remain legacy-only after Phase 2 by design, because relabelling a volume would mean destroying its data (see the P3 entry gate in the runbook)
behaviour of a container whose entrypoint is a relative image default and whose arguments were overridden at creation; that shape is blocked by the equivalence gate rather than migrated
Phase 3 removal of legacy writes or reads

detail.probeShape: legacy-only container seeded with the raw CLI, running, holding one legacy-only named volume at /data
detail.sentinel: written into the named volume before the sweep, read back unchanged after the replacement and again after a stop/start cycle
detail.scoping: the sweep was restricted with Only to the probe identity, so the five old-only managed containers on the same host were not targets

detail.seeded: a second container carrying com.mrbaron3.workflow.agentopsctl=v1 and com.mrbaron3.servo.agentopsctl=v2
detail.observed: Apply returned an error, report.Applied was false, and the probe remained legacy-only with its named volume still attached and still present

optInGate.observed: both cases SKIP, which is why an opted-in run with a missing prerequisite fails instead of skipping

probeCleanup.policy: every probe resource carries a prefix unique to the process; cleanup deletes those exact identities and never selects by label
probeCleanup.verificationCommand: container list --all --format json / container volume list --format json / container network list --format json filtered for the labelp2 prefix

hostMigration.targetSelection: exact identities passed to --only; --apply refuses an empty or duplicated set

runs.outcome: all four migrated; all remained stopped; 24 of 24 stages ok

guardProbes.note: these runs are recorded because they exercise the fail-closed guards on the real host, not because they migrated anything
guardProbes.broadApply: agentopsctl migrate-labels --apply (no --only) exited 1 without contacting a single container
guardProbes.duplicateApply: agentopsctl migrate-labels --apply --only agentops-runner,agentops-runner exited 1; its halted sweep record is evidence/label-p2/sweep-20260810T051624Z.json

volumePreservation.observed: all 23 named volumes present before and after; the five volumes attached to migrated containers were re-attached at the same destinations with the same read-only flags

restartReconciliation.observed: started after migration, reported dual ownership and role labels, re-attached agentops-postgres-data at /var/lib/postgresql, and its PostgreSQL 18 data cluster (PG_VERSION=18) was intact; returned to stopped

rollback.predicate: every migrated container still carries com.mrbaron3.workflow.agentopsctl=v1 plus its legacy role and spec-sha256, so the pre-migration binary continues to discover it
rollback.perStage: documented in docs/runbooks/container-label-migration.md; the only window in which a container does not exist is between delete and recreate, and the named volume and its data are untouched throughout
